text: Epigenetic modification of DNA located in germ cells alters the levels of gene expression for loci expressing proteins involved in sperm development, with resulting impaired spermatogenesis causing lower sperm counts, problems in sperm function, and other sperm abnormalities (for review of normal epigenetic modifications in spermatogenesis, see Gunes and Kulac (2013), for review of how disruption of epigenetic modifications disrupts spermatogenesis, see Cui et al. (2025)).
